items.title: Ruth Lion interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998
items.q: Yeah. Meade Lux Lewis and Albert Ammons. And so he went backstage.

ctx.x: Sure, they did the piano duets there.

Yeah. Meade Lux Lewis and Albert Ammons. And so he went backstage. I can get a little bit of the feeling that he must have had. I mean because when you hear this record, even though today we might consider it dated but it had such a vitality to it. And Alfred being a person who reacted immediately to something that he really liked, he went backstage and he said, “I belong to a club of people who love jazz. Would you make a twelve-inch record so you wouldn’t have to stop playing? You could just play and play and…

We talked a little bit on the phone a couple of times about what it was about African American musicians especially that seemed to attract him. Do you feel that it was a mission for him to promote their music and record it? Or what was it?
